questions.template: How many lines of symmetry does a SQUARE have?
questions.hint: Fold it top-to-bottom, side-to-side… and across BOTH diagonals!
questions.explain: A square folds perfectly 4 ways: 2 through the middles and 2 through the corners.

questions.template: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry: A, F or G?
questions.hint: Imagine folding each letter down the middle — which halves match?
questions.explain: A folds left-onto-right perfectly. F and G have no matching fold.

questions.template: A rectangle (not a square) has how many lines of symmetry?
questions.hint: Middles yes — but the diagonal folds DON'T match!
questions.explain: Only the two middle folds work. Diagonal folds tip the halves apart.

questions.template: An equilateral triangle (all sides equal) has how many lines of symmetry?
questions.hint: One fold through each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
questions.explain: Three equal sides give three perfect folds — one per corner.

questions.template: Which letter has TWO lines of symmetry: H, T or L?
questions.hint: T only folds one way. L doesn't fold at all!
questions.explain: H folds both left-right AND top-bottom. T folds only left-right; L matches no fold.

questions.template: A regular hexagon has how many lines of symmetry?
questions.hint: Regular shapes have as many fold-lines as sides!
questions.explain: Regular polygons hide a rule: lines of symmetry = number of sides. Hexagon → 6.

questions.template: A cog has {n} identical teeth spaced evenly. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.hint: Same rule as regular shapes — one line per tooth.
questions.explain: Evenly-spaced identical teeth give {n} perfect folds. Symmetry keeps cogs balanced so they don't wobble!
